dossier.deep_context:
# 2018-2910 — Jack in the Bot: Kayla

A swerve robot with a cube elevator is documented by its CAD release and technical team replies. The strongest reviewed details concern protected internal belt rigging, separate shift/lock functions, absolute azimuth sensing and auxiliary traversal wheels. Public render geometry is a reference; complete CAD dimensions and every intake revision are not audited here.

## Strategic interpretation

Kayla illustrates the distinction between elegant packaging and service cost. A hidden belt run protects against snagging yet the team estimated a substantial replacement procedure. The source also gives a precise material/failure sequence rather than a generic claim that belts always survive climbing.

## Protected belt-in-tube elevator and failure correction

Version: Kayla released 2018 CAD discussion. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095. Physical PDF pages: not applicable; see source locators.

Source locators:

- Post 6: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/6
- Post 13: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/13

### Published construction or code

Team replies describe a belt routed inside elevator tubes. A build-season fiberglass-cord belt failed at a sharp carriage attachment during a hard-stop event. The team removed the edge and changed to steel tensile cord, reporting no further such failure at the time. A replacement was estimated at about 45 minutes. Separate cylinders shift lift gearing and lock the elevator after climbing.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Protect the drive path from snagging and avoid managing cable tracking on a spool; the author also says the initial CAD arrangement seemed workable and was built.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not rewrite this as a fully optimized belt selection study. Two changes occurred together, so the failure account does not isolate belt material from the eliminated cut edge. Service labor is part of architecture cost even if replacement is mechanically straightforward. For 1833, the useful geometric routing does not permit copying pneumatic shift/lock actuation. Derive whether one fixed electric reduction plus a positive latch can cover both duties, or whether a separate climb drive is warranted.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Inspect terminations, bend radii, hard-stop control and access for threading replacement. Estimate a realistic recovery time and verify the new load/actuation envelope.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Kayla CAD release whole-robot render](../../images/history_2018-2910_source.jpg)

## Sideways platform traversal and absolute module position

Version: Kayla released 2018 CAD discussion. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095. Physical PDF pages: not applicable; see source locators.

Source locators:

- Post 6: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/6
- Post 8: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/8
- Post 18: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/18
- Post 19: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095/19

### Published construction or code

The team identifies water-jetted 6061-T6 auxiliary wheels intended to reduce bottoming when moving sideways across the platform. It confirms absolute azimuth encoders and discusses module bearing selection. The release does not supply a complete, independently checked obstacle-success rate.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Avoid getting stranded during sideways travel and retain known module position between matches.

### Engineering interpretation

Swerve enables lateral motion but does not erase chassis breakover geometry. A belly support that works in one direction may expose another edge or reduce traction when loaded. Absolute position also needs a valid physical offset and a detectable sensor fault; it is not proof calibration is unnecessary. The transferable decision is to check the motion direction against field obstacles and preserve known heading at startup.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Use coarse contact geometry for every traversal orientation and the expected lift state. Validate the uncertain high-centering case; verify sensor offset and failure recovery separately from the mechanical bearing design.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Kayla CAD release whole-robot render](../../images/history_2018-2910_source.jpg)

## Remaining evidence gaps

- Curated historical mechanism cohort, not a top-25 EPA selection; no EPA/rank fabricated.
- Selected primary publications and figures reviewed; no narrated-video review or exact CAD verification is claimed.
- Historical pneumatic/turret hardware is retained as fact but disallowed in new 1833 recommendations. Adaptation requires new interface/load/holding/recovery analysis.
- No exhaustive every-version certification, new PCH performance benchmark or match-by-match Einstein tactical audit.

binder_audit.interpretation: Curated historical technical study; EPA not retrieved; selected pages/posts/code reviewed. No exhaustive binder-discovery or competition-version certification.

source_reviews.title: 2910 CAD Release 2018
source_reviews.locator: Posts 1, 6, 8, 13, 14 and 16–19; published render in post 1
source_reviews.review_basis: Read original release replies and visually inspected the corpus copy of the team render.
source_reviews.facts: The team documents internal belt routing and a build-season belt failure, shift and lock cylinders, passive platform wheels, thin-section X-contact steering bearings, and effectively one-to-one absolute azimuth sensing.
source_reviews.limitations: The render is a single view of the released design. No assembly file, footage or competition software was inspected.

source_reviews.title: FRC Design Handbook reference 28
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the independent description of the cube handoff and static lift hooks; compared visible layout with team render.
source_reviews.facts: Identifies a through-bumper orientation intake and separate carriage roller claw on a two-stage continuous lift, with hooks used for climb.
source_reviews.limitations: Secondary description. Its speculative wheel-change rationale and spooled-lift label are excluded in favor of the team's belt account.

source_reviews.title: Team 2910 Competition History
source_reviews.facts: Identifies the robot as Kayla, describes maneuverability as the drive objective and lists the 2018 championship division and finalist outcome.
source_reviews.limitations: Season retrospective gives no individual cycle metrics.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Kayla combines a low through-bumper cube path, a separate elevator-mounted scoring tool and a swerve chassis. The lift drive sits out of the piece path by routing the belt through the tubes. The same mast provides endgame lift capacity by switching gearbox range and locking after climb. Its distinctive integration problem is to fit the intake opening, side-clearance rollers, steering modules and mast base in the same chassis without making the internal lift drive impractical to repair.
piece_flow: A floor cube enters the central bumper opening. Lower rollers draw and orient it into the receiving space of the roller claw, which travels independently on the carriage. This sequence is described in the handbook and the two roller heights are visible in the team render. Exact roller commands and handoff confirmation are undocumented.

The carriage takes the cube to plate height, and the claw's driven contact provides the release interface. The low pickup pose needs enough overlap for both assemblies to control an imperfectly centered cube without trapping it as the carriage leaves.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The chassis can translate sideways without rotating its intake away from a target. The team added two unpowered rollers at the mast base for sideways crossing of the platform. The belt's protected route leaves usable volume around the mast and keeps loose objects away from the drive element, but replacement requires splitting the stages. The published render shows upper hooks near the mast crossmember and the lower intake inside the front bumper gap.

subsystems.name: Swerve and azimuth feedback
subsystems.construction: Custom modules with thin-section X-contact bearings and MA3 absolute sensors. The steering output and encoder branch have equivalent gearing.
subsystems.operation: The sensor reports module orientation across power cycles. The team confirmed that an effectively one-to-one encoder relationship avoids routine re-zeroing.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted freedom to maneuver around field obstacles and considered the game suitable for swerve.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Absolute angle preserves the datum only while the keyed or geared relationship holds. Offset changes or encoder gear slip can bias both steering and any inferred chassis motion.
subsystems.interfaces: The bearing carries steering-axis loads, while calibration ties encoder angle to the actual wheel direction.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Recheck the mechanical and software datum after module replacement. Check wheel clearance at full steering sweep near bumper brackets.
subsystems.unknowns: Drive motor feedback and quantitative accuracy under load.

subsystems.name: Cube collector and carriage claw
subsystems.construction: Through-bumper floor rollers and a separate belt-and-wheel roller claw visible at the lowered mast, described in the handbook.
subsystems.operation: The floor mechanism orients the incoming cube and the claw takes it vertically to the switch or scale.
subsystems.team_rationale: The handbook ties this arrangement to varied cube orientations. A firsthand team comparison for this choice was not located.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A transfer can reduce raised collector mass but needs a stable orientation after asymmetric contact. A miscentered cube can wedge between stationary rollers and the moving receiver.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper gap, roller contact height and carriage home position jointly define admission and handoff.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect roller compliance and repeat the transfer after collision or carriage service.
subsystems.unknowns: Wheel revision chronology, retention force, home sensing and recovery behavior.

subsystems.name: Belt lift and climb
subsystems.construction: Continuous two-stage lift with belt routed around bearing pulleys through tubes. Separate pneumatic cylinders shift range and lock the elevator. Upper hooks visible in the release render.
subsystems.operation: High range handles cube placement. Low range handles climbing, and the separate lock holds after climb.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team favored belt protection and avoiding spool-tracking concerns.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The hard-stop event shows why clamp-edge radius and terminal impact matter independently of nominal belt strength. A climb changes loads at the carriage attachment, mast guides and lock.
subsystems.interfaces: The fixed end on the carriage, internal pulley path, gearbox and lock share responsibility for load transfer.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Team reports about 45 minutes to replace a belt, including removing guide bearings, separating stages and threading without twist.
subsystems.unknowns: Lock geometry, full belt specification, climb qualification and confirmed climb states.

subsystems.name: Sideways platform clearance
subsystems.construction: Two waterjet-cut 6061-T6 free rollers at the base of the elevator.
subsystems.operation: They provide rolling contact at the platform rather than letting the chassis settle on a fixed low surface.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team reports fewer instances of bottoming out, with occasional sticking still possible.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A passive roller only helps while driven wheels retain normal force and torque.
subsystems.interfaces: Wheel vector, platform edge and roller axis must align with the crossing direction.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check roller bearings and mounts for strikes and inspect whether damage reduces floor clearance.
subsystems.unknowns: Tested crossing angles and loaded ground clearance.

revisions: A fiberglass tensile-cord belt failed after a hard-stop strike cut it at a sharp carriage fixture. Team removed the edge and switched to steel tensile cord, reporting no recurrence through the release discussion.
transferable_principles: Design access before hiding a transmission inside structural tubes. Budget a sacrificial or rolling contact surface where a known obstacle intersects the chassis envelope.
disconfirming_conditions: The belt package loses value if inspection requires excessive disassembly or a termination cannot tolerate the load case. Side rollers cannot recover a route that unloads the driven wheels.
remaining_gaps: No event-specific hardware map, complete climb load path, match configuration of roller wheels or pickup software.

recommended_images.reason: Team render showing the central floor opening, carriage, upper hooks and passive rollers.
